summary: Fourteen days of Nightscout data with good CGM coverage (98.7 percent, 5-minute cadence, largest gap 65 minutes). Overall time in range 86.0 percent, average 121.6 mg/dL, coefficient of variation 32.6 percent, time above range 8.9 percent, time below range 5.1 percent. The dominant pattern is a broad daytime plateau in local time (10:00 to 17:00, peaking at 162.8 mg/dL at 16:00 with 32.1 percent above range) that resolves into concentrated low-glucose exposure at 18:00 to 19:00 (15.3 percent below range at 19:00) and again from 22:00 to 03:00 (18.5 percent below range at 01:00). No carbohydrate entries exist in the period, so all meal coverage is delivered reactively by UAM and SMB after glucose is already rising. Dynamic ISF is active with autosens disabled, and observed variable sensitivity spans 27.8 to 124 mg/dL/U against a flat profile ISF of 56 mg/dL/U, routing unannounced meals into the most aggressive part of the sensitivity curve. Observed insulin-on-board peaks of 4.73 and 5.94 U never approached the configured max IOB of 25 U, so that ceiling provided no braking before the two level-2 low clusters on 08-13 and 08-14. Three GLP-1 1.25 mg doses (08-14, 08-17, 08-20) and pump occlusion and error announcements on 08-19 are uncontrolled confounders.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM coverage is good and supports hourly and daily aggregation: 3995 valid entries against 4046 expected, 98.7 percent coverage, 5-minute cadence, zero invalid, zero duplicate and zero out-of-period entries, 10 gaps with a largest gap of 65 minutes. The first day (08-07, 33 readings) and last day (08-21, 269 readings) are partial and must not be compared at day level. Local timezone is BST at UTC plus 60 minutes, and hourly_glucose_local is a verified plus one hour shift of hourly_glucose. The profile is structurally complete: 7 basal segments, 5 carb-ratio segments, 1 flat ISF segment, 3 target segments and DIA. Scheduled basal totals 16.2 U per day, matching the profile-switch label of 16 to 2 U per day. Carbohydrate telemetry is entirely absent: carb_entries 0, total_carbs_g 0.0, carb_treatment_entries empty, extended_carb_entries 0, and COB 0 in every sampled loop status. Only a sample of telemetry is included (24 of 6214 device statuses, 40 of 2315 treatments, 24 therapy response windows). Loop reason strings contain constructs not represented in decision_inventory (UAM Boost 1 and 2, prTrial, twin, antBackout, accelMeal, Dosing sensitivity), indicating a customised build whose behaviour exceeds the supplied settings inventory. Logged target_bg values range from 80 to 116 mg/dL while the profile declares 90, 100 and 90 mg/dL and both autosens target flags are false.

analysis_steps.findings: Time below range of 5.1 percent exceeds the commonly used 4 percent threshold while coefficient of variation of 32.6 percent is acceptable. Low-glucose exposure is clock-clustered in local time: 18:00 at 7.7 percent, 19:00 at 15.3 percent, 22:00 at 6.6 percent, 23:00 at 10.1 percent, 00:00 at 11.4 percent, 01:00 at 18.5 percent, 02:00 at 10.1 percent and 03:00 at 10.2 percent, while 07:00 to 17:00 is nearly free of lows. Two sustained level-2 clusters occurred: 08-13 from 17:59 to 18:14 local (51, 47, 42, 45 mg/dL) and 08-14 from 19:04 to 19:14 local (48, 41, 41 mg/dL), both directly after high-glucose afternoons. An isolated 42 mg/dL at 08-21 07:19 local sits in an otherwise low-risk hour and may be artefact. Level-2 highs occurred on 08-15 (286 to 293) and 08-18 (285 to 290). Worst days were 08-14 (70.8 percent in range) and 08-18 (71.9 percent in range with 12.8 percent below range). Insulin-on-board reached 4.73 U at BG 262 and 5.94 U at BG 245.7, with variable sensitivity of 37.9 and 27.8 mg/dL/U and insulin requirement of 1.98 and 2.12 U. Lows recur despite frequent zero-rate temporary basals of 10 to 55 minutes, indicating that lows are driven by insulin already on board rather than concurrent basal flow. Confounders: GLP-1 1.25 mg on 08-14, 08-17 and 08-20; occlusion and pump error announcements on 08-19; site changes on 08-10, 08-13 and 08-17; sensor changes on 08-11 and 08-21.

analysis_steps.findings: The only genuinely fasting-like window, 04:00 to 07:00 local, is the best-controlled part of the day: averages 99.5 to 106 mg/dL, 95.2 to 98.7 percent in range and 1.3 to 4.8 percent below range. This does not indicate a basal defect. The 00:00 to 03:00 low exposure is not a clean fasting signal because it follows evening correction and UAM activity carried by a 10-hour DIA. The high plateau from 14:00 to 17:00 local coincides with the lowest scheduled basal segment (16:00 at 0.5 U/h), and the 18:00 to 19:00 low window coincides with basal stepping back up to 0.6 and 0.7 U/h, but with zero carbohydrate records an unlogged afternoon intake is an equally plausible driver and the pattern cannot be attributed to the basal shape. The morning rise from 99.5 mg/dL at 07:00 to 148.0 mg/dL at 10:00 sits inside the highest basal segment (0.8 U/h) with zero percent below range; dawn effect and unlogged breakfast cannot be separated. Profile targets cannot be validated because effective target_bg in the sampled statuses ranges from 80 to 116 mg/dL, systematically lower at high glucose and higher at low-glucose risk, which is not explained by the three profile target segments or by the six temporary targets and not by autosens, since both autosens target flags are false. A further constraint is that any increase to a profile basal segment would raise the automation ceiling, because the binding clamp observed is maxSafeBasal of 4 U/h derived from max_daily_safety_multiplier 5.0 times the largest basal segment.

analysis_steps.findings: Carb ratios of 13, 11.1, 13.2, 10.5 and 12.6 g/U cannot be evaluated at all, because no carbohydrate was entered in 14 days and COB is zero in every sampled status, so no carb ratio segment was ever exercised. The flat profile ISF of 56 mg/dL/U is not the operative sensitivity: dynamic sensitivity is enabled at an adjustment factor of 70 percent with autosens disabled, and observed variable_sens spans 27.8 to 124 mg/dL/U, roughly 2.2 times weaker than profile at low glucose (124 at BG 69.8, 111.9 at BG 95.1) and roughly 2 times stronger at high glucose with high insulin-on-board (37.9 at BG 262 with 4.73 U, 27.8 at BG 245.7 with 5.94 U). Therapy response windows cannot yield an ISF estimate because the listed bolus is never the only insulin acting: 0.2 U from 234 to 56 mg/dL at 120 minutes on 08-14, 0.65 U from 264 to 96 mg/dL on 08-19, and conversely 0.2 U from 100 to 235 mg/dL at 240 minutes on 08-14. Directionally these show overshoot after high-glucose corrections and under-response after low-glucose boluses, consistent with the dynamic sensitivity gradient, but they are quantitatively unusable. DIA of 10 hours with free_peak_oref insulin leaves 11 of 23 sampled windows still net negative at 360 minutes, which is compatible with a long action tail but equally compatible with concurrent basal and UAM activity, so DIA cannot be validated or refuted here.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are both enabled and, in the absence of any carbohydrate entry, they constitute the entire meal-coverage mechanism; every sampled dosing decision is UAM-driven. There is no duplicate COB counting, because COB is zero throughout. Among activation conditions, smb_always_enabled true makes smb_with_cob_enabled false and smb_after_carbs_enabled false effectively inert, which is redundancy rather than a defect, while smb_with_temp_target_enabled true combined with smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled false is the protective pairing and was actively used through six temporary targets. The material finding concerns SMB strength: with basal segments of 0.5 to 0.8 U/h, max_uam_smb_basal_minutes of 20 implies a per-SMB cap near 0.17 to 0.27 U, and the package confirms standardMaxBolus 0.2 on 08-07. However the delivered SMB repeatedly exceeded that base, for example 0.4 U on 08-07 with UAM Boost 2 of 1.57, an increased SMB percentage on 08-18, and 1.6 U on 08-19 under UAM High Boost, roughly seven to eight times the base cap. The boost multipliers are not represented in decision_inventory, so the configured minutes are the base that boosts multiply rather than the delivered limit. The interval of 3 minutes is read directly from raw_settings and not inferred from any waiting message; combined with boosted SMB size and temporary basal to the 4 U/h clamp it permits the observed accumulation to 4.73 and 5.94 U of insulin-on-board.

analysis_steps.findings: Autosens is disabled and dynamic sensitivity is enabled at 70 percent with both target-adjustment flags false; autosens state is taken from configuration and not inferred from sensitivity_ratio, which is a neutral 1 in 18 of 24 sampled statuses and below 1 in six (0.98, 0.94, 0.92, 0.91, 0.88 and 0.79), values that must originate from the dynamic path since autosens is off. Max basal of 12 U/h is not the binding limit: the observed clamp is maxSafeBasal 4 U/h on 08-14, produced by the internal daily safety multiplier of 5.0 applied to the largest basal segment of 0.8 U/h, so the form value never acts and would only matter if profile basal rose steeply. Max IOB of 25 U is the material concern: it is roughly 125 percent of an estimated 20 U per day total insulin and about 1.5 times the 16.2 U per day scheduled basal, and observed peak insulin-on-board of 5.94 U never approached it, so it provided no braking in any cycle including those preceding the level-2 low clusters of 08-13 and 08-14. On dynamic ISF, the quantitative link to the low-glucose pattern is that at 08-21 21:09 a sensitivity of 27.8 mg/dL/U produced an insulin requirement of 2.12 U, roughly double the requirement implied by the profile ISF of 56, an excess corresponding to about 110 mg/dL of additional expected fall, which matches observed overshoots of minus 178, minus 168 and minus 153 mg/dL that each began in the 14:00 to 17:00 local high window and ended in the 18:00 to 19:00 local low window. A competing explanation is not excluded: unlogged carbohydrate still absorbing at dosing time would justify a large dose with overshoot appearing only when absorption ended. The build formula and its neutral point are not supplied, so the direction of any factor change is reasoned from the observed output spread rather than from the number itself. The carbohydrate absorption model, min_5m_carbimpact of 8 and meal_max_absorption_hours of 7, acts only when COB exceeds zero and is therefore inert across the whole period, with no evidence available to tune it.

analysis_steps.findings: User declaration and telemetry agree and do not conflict. The declaration container aaps_profile.analysis_context exists with source declared_by_user and declared_at 2026-08-21T21:08:10, and its meal_strategies list is an empty array, period_exceptions is null and strategy_stable_for_period is null. Because strategy_stable_for_period is null rather than true, no value may be treated as a representative declaration for the period, so applicability and confidence are limited throughout this stage. Telemetry corroborates: zero carb entries, zero extended-carb entries, all 24 therapy response windows flagged is_extended_carbs false and typed Correction Bolus, and COB zero in all sampled statuses. Observed execution is a single consistent pattern: no meal announcement, no prebolus and no up-front meal bolus, with coverage delivered reactively after the rise begins by UAM SMB and high temporary basal, plus occasional small manual corrections. Representative examples in local time: 0.2 U at BG 100 on 08-14 at 11:25 followed by 235 mg/dL at 240 minutes and 231 at 360 minutes; 0.1 U at 110 on 08-09 at 10:01 followed by 161 at 120 minutes; 0.25 U at 118 on 08-16 at 08:50 followed by 154 at 360 minutes; 0.05 U at BG 245 on 08-21 at 22:09 while insulin-on-board was already 5.94 U. The daytime shape is one broad nine-hour plateau with two shoulders rather than discrete sharp meal spikes, consistent either with several overlapping unannounced eating occasions or with slower flatter absorption, the latter plausible because GLP-1 1.25 mg was dosed on 08-14, 08-17 and 08-20; these cannot be separated. The consequence for the profile system is that every meal is handled through the correction pathway, where dynamic sensitivity collapses to 27.8 to 42.5 mg/dL/U at the elevated glucose the plateau produces, which is the first link in the overshoot chain.

analysis_steps.findings: No comparison between regular carbohydrates and extended carbohydrates is possible: carb_entries is 0, extended_carb_entries is 0, average_extended_carb_duration_min is null, carb_treatment_entries is empty and is_extended_carbs is false in all 24 windows. No extended-carbohydrate amount, start offset or duration can be assessed or proposed, and none may be inferred from an aggregate average. Extended carbohydrates in AAPS are a carbohydrate announcement spread over time that shapes COB and predictions, and are not a pump extended or dual-wave bolus, so they deliver no insulin themselves. The only absorption-adjacent quantity measurable without carbohydrate entries is observed glucose action time: unannounced daytime excursions run roughly six to nine hours from first rise near 08:00 local to baseline near 19:00 local, with individual windows still elevated at 240 to 360 minutes. This long observed action time is directionally compatible with meal_max_absorption_hours of 7 and with GLP-1 delayed emptying, but it is confounded by overlapping eating occasions, corrections, temporary basals and the 10-hour DIA tail, so it does not validate that setting. The carbohydrate absorption group therefore remains inert and would only become observable after carbohydrate logging begins.

analysis_steps.findings: Competing explanations resolve as follows. The leading account is a late-day over-correction cascade: unannounced meals produce a broad plateau, dynamic sensitivity at elevated glucose falls to 27.8 to 42.5 mg/dL/U, boosted UAM SMB and temporary basal to the 4 U/h clamp accumulate 4.7 to 5.9 U of insulin-on-board with no effective max IOB brake, and the 10-hour DIA tail carries that insulin into the 18:00 to 19:00 and 22:00 to 03:00 local low windows. Supporting evidence is the pairing of a 162.8 mg/dL peak at 16:00 with 15.3 percent below range at 19:00, both level-2 low clusters immediately following high afternoons, and repeated large negative swings after small logged corrections. The competing account of an evening or overnight basal excess is weakened because lows recur despite frequent zero-rate temporary basals, though it is not excluded for 00:00 to 03:00. The competing account of an afternoon basal shortfall is complicated rather than resolved: automation already reaches its safety clamp in that window, so a basal increase would be partly redundant, and raising the largest basal segment would also raise the 5 times clamp, which conflicts with the low-glucose constraint. Unlogged carbohydrate still absorbing at dosing time remains a genuine alternative to an overly aggressive sensitivity gradient and cannot be separated with this data. The resulting safe order places one non-insulin, non-delivery action first, then a single ceiling change that truncates only extremes, and defers every dependent sensitivity and SMB change to later single steps. No profile row changes, because the fasting-like window is well controlled, carb ratios were never exercised, the profile ISF is not the operative sensitivity, DIA cannot be validated, and the effective target is generated by the build rather than by the profile target segments.

strengths: CGM data quality is strong and supports the analysis: 98.7 percent coverage, consistent 5-minute cadence, zero invalid, duplicate or out-of-period entries, and a largest gap of only 65 minutes.

Overall glycaemic metrics are good, with 86.0 percent time in range, an average of 121.6 mg/dL and a coefficient of variation of 32.6 percent, which is within the commonly used 36 percent stability threshold.

The fasting-like window from 04:00 to 07:00 local is the best-controlled part of the day, with averages of 99.5 to 106 mg/dL, 95.2 to 98.7 percent in range and only 1.3 to 4.8 percent below range, indicating that the overnight basal foundation is broadly appropriate.
The loop responds actively and defensively to falling glucose, issuing frequent zero-rate temporary basals of 10 to 55 minutes well before predicted lows.

SMB activation conditions are set to a protective combination, with SMB permitted under ordinary temporary targets but suppressed under high temporary targets, and the user actively employed six temporary targets during the period.
The profile is structurally complete and internally coherent, with 7 basal segments totalling 16.2 U per day that match the profile-switch label, plus defined carb ratio, ISF, target and DIA values.
Site changes, sensor changes and pump events are annotated, which allowed several isolated extreme values to be attributed to hardware rather than to therapy settings.

issues.title: Clock-clustered low-glucose exposure above the recommended threshold
issues.detail: Time below range is 5.1 percent overall, above the commonly used 4 percent target, and it concentrates in two local-time windows: 18:00 to 19:00 (7.7 and 15.3 percent) and 22:00 to 03:00 (6.6, 10.1, 11.4, 18.5, 10.1 and 10.2 percent). Two sustained level-2 clusters occurred on 08-13 (51, 47, 42, 45 mg/dL) and 08-14 (48, 41, 41 mg/dL), each immediately after a high-glucose afternoon.

issues.title: Large insulin-on-board accumulation without an effective ceiling
issues.detail: Sampled insulin-on-board reached 4.73 U at BG 262 and 5.94 U at BG 245.7, roughly 30 percent of an estimated daily insulin picture, while max IOB is configured at 25 U and was therefore never approached. The configured ceiling provided no braking in the cycles preceding the level-2 low clusters.

issues.title: Very wide effective sensitivity range driven by dynamic ISF
issues.detail: With autosens disabled and dynamic sensitivity enabled at 70 percent, observed variable sensitivity spans 27.8 to 124 mg/dL/U against a flat profile ISF of 56 mg/dL/U. At 27.8 mg/dL/U the loop requested 2.12 U where the profile ISF implies roughly half that, an excess corresponding to about 110 mg/dL of additional expected fall, matching observed overshoots of minus 178, minus 168 and minus 153 mg/dL.

issues.title: Broad daytime hyperglycaemic plateau covered only reactively
issues.detail: Local hours 10:00 to 17:00 average 132 to 163 mg/dL with time above range up to 32.1 percent at 16:00. Because no carbohydrate is announced, all coverage is delivered after the rise has begun, which routes every eating occasion through the correction pathway at its most aggressive sensitivity.

issues.title: Delivered SMB size exceeds the configured base cap
issues.detail: With basal of 0.5 to 0.8 U/h, max_uam_smb_basal_minutes of 20 implies a base cap near 0.17 to 0.27 U and standardMaxBolus 0.2 is logged, yet delivered SMB reached 0.4 U under a boost of 1.57 and 1.6 U under UAM High Boost. The boost multipliers are not represented in the supplied settings inventory, so the configured value is a base that boosts scale rather than a delivered limit.

issues.title: Effective glucose target does not match the profile target schedule
issues.detail: Logged target_bg spans 80 to 116 mg/dL while the profile declares 90, 100 and 90 mg/dL and both autosens target flags are false. The pattern is systematic, near 80 at high glucose and 105 to 116 at low-glucose risk, indicating that the running build generates the effective target. Profile target evidence is therefore weak and target changes cannot be justified from this data.

issues.title: Uncontrolled physiological and hardware confounders
issues.detail: GLP-1 1.25 mg was dosed on 08-14, 08-17 and 08-20, overlapping the worst days and plausibly flattening and prolonging excursions, and occlusion plus pump error announcements on 08-19 precede that day's 264 mg/dL peak and its large negative swing. These episodes must not be used as evidence for or against any setting.

recommendations.title: Begin logging one recurring daytime eating occasion before changing any insulin setting
recommendations.description: No carbohydrate was entered in 14 days, so carb ratios were never exercised, COB was zero in every sampled status, and the entire daytime plateau from 10:00 to 17:00 local was covered reactively by UAM after glucose was already rising. This single gap blocks carb ratio assessment, blocks assessment of the carbohydrate absorption model, prevents separating an afternoon basal shortfall from unlogged intake, and initiates the sequence that ends in low glucose at 18:00 to 19:00 and 22:00 to 03:00 local. Logging changes no insulin delivery setting and adds no insulin exposure, which makes it the lowest-risk first action while carrying the highest analytical yield.

suggested_change.review_after: 7 to 10 days of paired carbohydrate and glucose data

recommendations.title: Discuss tightening the max IOB ceiling so that it can act as a real brake
recommendations.description: Max IOB is configured at 25 U while observed peak insulin-on-board was 5.94 U, roughly 125 percent of an estimated 20 U daily insulin picture and about 1.5 times the 16.2 U per day scheduled basal. Because it was never approached, it applied no restraint in the cycles that preceded the level-2 low clusters of 08-13 and 08-14. A ceiling truncates only extreme accumulation and does not alter routine dosing, so it is the least disruptive of the automation options. The exact value must be sized with the care team because total daily dose is bounded only between roughly 20 and 36 U per day in this package.

suggested_change.basis: observed peak insulin-on-board 5.94 U with headroom
suggested_change.depends_on: confirmation of true total daily dose

recommendations.title: Keep dynamic ISF unchanged for now and reassess only after carbohydrate logging
recommendations.description: The dynamic sensitivity gradient is the leading mechanistic explanation for the overshoot pattern, but it cannot yet be separated from the alternative that unlogged carbohydrate was still absorbing when large doses were given, which would justify those doses. The build formula and its neutral point are not supplied, so the correct direction of a factor change cannot be derived from the value of 70 percent itself. Changing it now would also alter the same variable that carbohydrate logging is intended to clarify.

suggested_change.reassess_after: carbohydrate logging plus the max IOB review
suggested_change.condition_to_revisit: overshoot after high-glucose corrections persists with carbohydrates announced

recommendations.title: Hold the UAM SMB strength setting as the last resort in the sequence
recommendations.description: Reducing max_uam_smb_basal_minutes would lower the base that boost multipliers scale, but it is downstream of dynamic sensitivity, which determines the insulin requirement that the cap truncates. Reducing it before the earlier steps would also weaken the only mechanism currently covering the 10:00 to 17:00 local plateau, where time above range reaches 32.1 percent, and would risk trading low glucose for high glucose.

suggested_change.position_in_sequence: after carbohydrate logging, max IOB and any dynamic ISF review
suggested_change.condition_to_revisit: low glucose at 18:00 to 19:00 and 22:00 to 03:00 local persists after earlier steps

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep all 17 profile rows at their current values, including every basal segment, and verify the basal shape with one deliberate fasting observation across the 14:00 to 20:00 local window before considering any basal edit.
profile_recommendation.rationale: The only genuinely fasting-like window, 04:00 to 07:00 local, is the best-controlled part of the day at 99.5 to 106 mg/dL with 95.2 to 98.7 percent in range, so the overnight basal foundation is supported by the data. The apparent pairing of the 0.5 U/h segment at 16:00 with the 162.8 mg/dL peak, and of the step up to 0.6 and 0.7 U/h with the 18:00 to 19:00 lows, is confounded by the complete absence of carbohydrate records, by boosted UAM dosing reaching the 4 U/h safety clamp in that same window and by a 10-hour DIA tail. Raising the largest basal segment would also raise the automation ceiling, since the observed clamp of 4 U/h equals the daily safety multiplier of 5.0 times the largest basal rate, which conflicts with the requirement not to increase insulin exposure between 14:00 and 03:00 local. Carb ratios were never exercised, the profile ISF of 56 mg/dL/U is not the operative sensitivity because dynamic ISF produced 27.8 to 124 mg/dL/U, DIA cannot be validated without an insulin-free window, and the effective target is generated by the build rather than by the profile target segments.
profile_recommendation.next_check: On a day with no eating between 12:00 and 20:00 local and no manual correction, record glucose every 30 minutes and note whether the 14:00 to 17:00 rise still appears and whether the 18:00 to 19:00 fall still appears; a rise without food would support the afternoon basal segment as a cause, while a flat profile would confirm that unannounced eating and the reactive dosing response are the drivers.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: local hours 00:00 to 03:00 show 11.4, 18.5, 10.1 and 10.2 percent below range, which looks like basal excess, but lows recur despite frequent zero-rate temporary basals of 10 to 55 minutes, meaning delivery was already suspended when the lows occurred. Uncertainty: the preceding evening carries a 10-hour DIA tail plus boosted UAM dosing, so the responsible insulin was delivered hours earlier. Dependencies: this row cannot be separated from dynamic ISF, max IOB and the absence of carbohydrate announcement, all of which are addressed earlier in the sequence; lowering it now would add a second simultaneous change and would probably not remove the cause.

Evidence: local hour 05:00 averages 104.2 mg/dL with 95.2 percent in range and 4.8 percent below range, and hour 06:00 averages 99.5 mg/dL with 97.5 percent in range, which is the best-performing window of the day. Uncertainty: minimal for this segment, since it sits in the only genuinely fasting-like period. Dependencies: none that would justify a change; altering a well-behaved segment would add noise to the verification of the earlier steps.

Evidence: local hours 06:00 and 07:00 average 99.5 mg/dL with 97.5 and 98.7 percent in range and only 2.5 and 1.3 percent below range. Uncertainty: an isolated 42 mg/dL at 08-21 07:19 local sits in an otherwise low-risk hour and may be a sensor artefact, so it does not support a reduction. Dependencies: this is the largest basal segment and therefore sets the observed automation clamp of 4 U/h through the daily safety multiplier of 5.0, so any change here would silently move an automation limit as well and must not be combined with automation changes.

Evidence: local hours 10:00 to 13:00 average 148.0, 132.3, 141.3 and 135.0 mg/dL with time above range from 7.5 to 20.2 percent, which could suggest under-basalisation. Uncertainty: no carbohydrate was entered in the period, so unannounced breakfast and midday eating is at least as plausible an explanation as the basal rate, and the loop already responds with temporary basals up to 2.7 U/h in this window. Dependencies: separating these two explanations requires the carbohydrate logging step first; a basal increase now would also raise insulin exposure ahead of the 18:00 to 19:00 low window.

Evidence: local hour 16:00 is the highest of the day at 162.8 mg/dL with 32.1 percent above range and zero percent below range, and it coincides exactly with the lowest scheduled basal segment. Uncertainty: this coincidence is not attributable to the basal rate, because automation already reaches its maxSafeBasal clamp of 4 U/h in this window, so additional scheduled basal would be partly redundant, and unannounced afternoon eating remains an equally plausible driver. Dependencies: the constraint that no change may increase insulin exposure between 14:00 and 03:00 local applies directly here, since this window feeds the 18:00 to 19:00 low period with 15.3 percent below range; the fasting observation named in profile_recommendation must resolve this first.

Evidence: local hour 18:00 shows 7.7 percent below range with a minimum of 42 mg/dL, and the step up from 0.5 to 0.6 U/h occurs at this boundary. Uncertainty: the level-2 clusters on 08-13 and 08-14 both began in this hour but followed high-glucose afternoons with boosted SMB and temporary basal, so the causal insulin was delivered earlier and is carried by the 10-hour DIA tail rather than by this segment. Dependencies: reducing this row would treat a symptom of the upstream accumulation identified in the automation stages and would confound the verification of the max IOB step.

Evidence: local hour 19:00 has the highest low-glucose exposure of the day at 15.3 percent below range with a minimum of 41 mg/dL, while averaging 105.4 mg/dL. Uncertainty: as in the 18:00 segment, zero-rate temporary basals were frequently already active when these lows occurred, which points to insulin-on-board of 4.7 to 5.9 U rather than to the scheduled rate. Dependencies: this is the strongest single candidate for a later basal reduction, but only if low glucose in this hour persists after carbohydrate logging and the max IOB review; changing it now would violate the one-change-at-a-time rule and mask which step produced any improvement.

Evidence: carb_entries is 0, total_carbs_g is 0.0, carb_treatment_entries is empty and COB is zero in all 24 sampled loop statuses, so this ratio was never applied to any dose during the period. Uncertainty: complete, since no observation exists that could support or refute the value. Dependencies: blocked by the meal_ecarbs_absorption stage; it becomes assessable only after the carbohydrate logging step produces paired carbohydrate and glucose data.

Evidence: no carbohydrate entry exists in the period and COB is zero throughout, so this segment was never exercised. Uncertainty: complete; the 04:00 to 08:00 window is also the quietest eating period, so it will be the last segment to gain evidence. Dependencies: requires carbohydrate logging before any assessment is possible.

Evidence: the morning rise from 99.5 mg/dL at 07:00 to 148.0 mg/dL at 10:00 local is consistent with unannounced breakfast, but with zero carbohydrate entries this ratio never acted on it. Uncertainty: dawn physiology and unannounced eating cannot be separated, and there is zero percent below range in these hours, so no safety pressure exists. Dependencies: assessment requires the carbohydrate logging step and, if breakfast is the recurring occasion chosen, this is the segment most likely to gain evidence first.

Evidence: this is the strongest ratio in the schedule and it aligns with the highest-glucose window at 16:00 local (162.8 mg/dL, 32.1 percent above range), yet it was never applied because no carbohydrate was announced. Uncertainty: complete regarding the ratio itself; the window's behaviour is currently explained by reactive UAM dosing rather than by any carbohydrate calculation. Dependencies: blocked by the absence of carbohydrate entries, and any future evaluation must also account for the low-glucose constraint in the following hours.

Evidence: no carbohydrate entry exists, so this segment never contributed to a dose; the evening pattern is dominated instead by carried insulin-on-board and small manual corrections such as 0.05 U at BG 245 with 5.94 U already on board on 08-21. Uncertainty: complete for the ratio. Dependencies: blocked until carbohydrate logging exists, and any evening change would additionally interact with the 22:00 to 03:00 low window.

Evidence: dynamic sensitivity is enabled with autosens disabled, and observed variable_sens ranged from 27.8 to 124 mg/dL/U, so the flat profile value is only one input to a glucose and insulin-on-board scaled calculation rather than the operative sensitivity. Uncertainty: the build formula and its neutral point are not supplied, so the effect of moving 56 in either direction cannot be predicted from the package. Dependencies: strictly coupled to the dynamic ISF adjustment factor; changing both would be a simultaneous change of dependent parameters, and the automation-side factor is the more direct lever, so the profile value is held.

Evidence: logged effective target_bg ranged from 80 to 116 mg/dL across sampled statuses while this segment declares 90, and both autosens target flags are false, so the running build is generating the effective target rather than this row. Uncertainty: high, because the mechanism is undocumented and only 24 of 6214 statuses are visible; a change to this row may not propagate as expected. Dependencies: target evidence remains weak until the effective-target mechanism is understood, so no target row may be moved on this data.

Evidence: this daytime target of 100 covers the plateau hours, yet sampled statuses in that window logged effective targets as low as 80 to 82 mg/dL at elevated glucose, which is not explained by this row or by the six temporary targets. Uncertainty: high for the same undocumented mechanism. Dependencies: raising this target could reduce afternoon dosing pressure, but that overlaps directly with the dynamic ISF and max IOB steps and would confound their verification, so it is withheld.

Evidence: this segment covers the 23:00 to 03:00 local window that carries 10.1 to 18.5 percent below range, which superficially argues for a higher overnight target. Uncertainty: the sampled statuses show the build already raising the effective target to 105 to 116 mg/dL when low-glucose risk is predicted, so the declared value is not what the loop uses, and the lows persisted despite that. Dependencies: the overnight lows are attributed primarily to insulin carried from the afternoon and evening, so this row is held until the upstream steps are verified.

Evidence: 11 of 23 sampled therapy response windows remain net negative at 360 minutes, for example minus 50, minus 51, minus 66 and minus 176 mg/dL, which is compatible with a long action tail. Uncertainty: those windows always contain concurrent basal, temporary basal and UAM SMB activity, so they cannot isolate insulin decay, and no insulin-free window exists in the period. Dependencies: DIA interacts with the insulin-on-board model that the max IOB step is intended to constrain; shortening DIA would reduce calculated insulin-on-board and could paradoxically increase dosing, so it must not be changed alongside the max IOB review.

Evidence: with zero carbohydrate entries and COB zero in every sampled status, SMB and UAM constitute the entire meal-coverage mechanism, and every sampled dosing decision is UAM-driven. There is no duplicate COB counting because COB is always zero. Uncertainty: whether UAM is over-reacting cannot be separated from the dynamic sensitivity gradient that sizes its requests. Dependencies: disabling either switch would remove all responsiveness to unannounced eating and would predictably worsen the 10:00 to 17:00 local plateau, where time above range reaches 32.1 percent, so both remain enabled while the upstream carbohydrate and ceiling steps are tested. Both components have values, so verify does not apply.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / SMB activation conditions (smb_always_enabled, smb_with_cob_enabled, smb_after_carbs_enabled, smb_with_temp_target_enabled, smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled)
parameter_decisions.rationale: Correction from earlier reasoning: the authoritative package values are smb_always_enabled true, smb_with_cob_enabled false, smb_after_carbs_enabled false, smb_with_temp_target_enabled true and smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled false, and the current_value string above is copied exactly from decision_inventory. Evidence: smb_always_enabled true makes the two carbohydrate-conditioned flags inert while COB is zero, which is redundancy rather than a defect, and the pairing of SMB permitted under ordinary temporary targets with SMB suppressed under high temporary targets is the protective configuration; the user set six temporary targets in the period and the largest sampled SMB of 1.6 U on 08-19 occurred after the relevant temporary target had expired, so no target was overridden. Uncertainty: only 24 of 6214 statuses are visible, so the frequency with which the high-target suppression engaged is unknown. Dependencies: the two carbohydrate-conditioned flags become observable only after carbohydrate logging begins, so they must be re-examined after that step rather than changed now. All components have values, so verify does not apply.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / SMB strength and frequency (smb_interval_minutes, max_smb_basal_minutes, max_uam_smb_basal_minutes)
parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: with basal of 0.5 to 0.8 U/h the 20-minute UAM allowance implies a base cap near 0.17 to 0.27 U, consistent with the logged standardMaxBolus of 0.2, yet delivered SMB reached 0.4 U under a boost of 1.57 and 1.6 U under UAM High Boost, so boost multipliers that are absent from the settings inventory dominate the delivered size. The 3-minute interval is read directly from raw_settings and not inferred from any waiting message. Uncertainty: because the boost logic and its own caps are undocumented, the effect of reducing the base minutes cannot be predicted precisely. Dependencies: this parameter is downstream of dynamic sensitivity, which determines the insulin requirement that the cap truncates, and it is the only mechanism currently covering the daytime plateau; reducing it before the carbohydrate and max IOB steps would risk trading low glucose for high glucose and would confound attribution. It is therefore held as the last item in the sequence. All components have values, so verify does not apply.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits (max_basal_u_per_hour, max_iob_units)
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: max_basal_u_per_hour=12 U/h; max_iob_units=6 to 8 U for review with the care team
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: observed peak insulin-on-board was 5.94 U at BG 245.7 on 08-21 and 4.73 U at BG 262 on 08-19, while max IOB is 25 U, roughly 125 percent of an estimated 20 U per day insulin picture and about 1.5 times the 16.2 U per day scheduled basal, so the ceiling was never approached and applied no restraint before the level-2 low clusters of 08-13 and 08-14. Max basal of 12 U/h is left unchanged because it is not the binding limit; the observed clamp is maxSafeBasal 4 U/h derived from the internal daily safety multiplier of 5.0 applied to the largest basal segment of 0.8 U/h. Uncertainty: total daily dose is bounded only between roughly 20 and 36 U per day because it is unclear whether total_insulin_u includes basal, so the suggested range is a discussion range and not a derived value, and a ceiling set too low could blunt legitimate coverage of the daytime plateau. Dependencies: chosen as the first insulin-related step because a ceiling truncates only extreme accumulation without altering routine dosing, and it must be changed alone, before any dynamic ISF or SMB strength change, so its effect on the 18:00 to 19:00 and 22:00 to 03:00 local windows can be attributed.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / Autosens and Dynamic ISF (autosens_enabled, dynamic_sensitivity_enabled, autosens_raises_target, autosens_lowers_target, dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent)
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: autosens state is taken from configuration, not inferred from sensitivity_ratio, which is a neutral 1 in 18 of 24 sampled statuses and below 1 in six, values that must arise from the dynamic path since autosens is off. Observed variable sensitivity spans 27.8 to 124 mg/dL/U against a flat profile ISF of 56, and at 27.8 the loop requested 2.12 U where the profile ISF implies roughly half, an excess of about 110 mg/dL of expected fall that matches observed overshoots of minus 178, minus 168 and minus 153 mg/dL beginning in the 14:00 to 17:00 local high window and ending in the 18:00 to 19:00 low window. Uncertainty: this is the leading but not the proven explanation, because unlogged carbohydrate still absorbing at dosing time would justify the same doses with overshoot appearing only when absorption ended, and the build formula and neutral point are not supplied, so the correct direction of a factor change cannot be derived from 70 percent itself. Dependencies: carbohydrate logging is designed to separate exactly these two explanations, and the max IOB ceiling is the safer first intervention, so this group is held and reassessed as the second insulin-related step, changed alone if at all. All components have values, so verify does not apply.

Evidence: both parameters act only when COB exceeds zero, and COB is zero in every sampled status with carb_entries 0 and extended_carb_entries 0, so neither parameter influenced any observed outcome in the period. Uncertainty: the observed six to nine hour daytime excursion span is directionally compatible with the 7-hour maximum absorption setting, but it is confounded by overlapping eating occasions, corrections, temporary basals, three GLP-1 doses and the 10-hour DIA tail, and no meal-linked evidence exists, so no duration may be inferred from it. Dependencies: these settings become live the moment carbohydrate is entered, so they must be re-examined after the carbohydrate logging step and never before it. Both components have values, so verify does not apply.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Consider announcing one recurring daytime eating occasion with an approximate carbohydrate amount entered at or shortly before the start of eating, while leaving every insulin-delivery setting unchanged, keeping SMB and UAM enabled exactly as they are, and not introducing extended carbohydrates in the same trial. A prebolus interval and an immediate bolus percentage cannot be proposed as numbers from this data, because no meal bolus exists to which either could apply and the declared meal strategy list is empty; the practical starting point is therefore announcement timing at the start of eating rather than a specified prebolus or split. Because smb_always_enabled is true, SMB continues to operate with carbohydrates on board, so announcement shifts the loop from late reactive UAM guessing toward earlier carb-ratio-informed dosing without adding a manual up-front bolus and without increasing total insulin exposure. Extended carbohydrates should be considered only after a regular carbohydrate entry has shown whether ordinary absorption fits the observed pattern, since extended carbohydrates are an announcement spread over time that shapes COB and predictions and are not a pump extended bolus.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Declared strategy and observed telemetry agree rather than conflict: aaps_profile.analysis_context has source declared_by_user with an empty meal_strategies array, period_exceptions null and strategy_stable_for_period null, and telemetry independently shows zero carbohydrate entries, zero extended-carbohydrate entries and COB zero in all sampled statuses. Observed execution is therefore fully reactive, with the daytime plateau from 10:00 to 17:00 local reaching 162.8 mg/dL at 16:00 with 32.1 percent above range, covered by boosted UAM SMB and temporary basal into a dynamic sensitivity of 27.8 to 42.5 mg/dL/U, producing insulin-on-board up to 5.94 U and low glucose concentrated at 18:00 to 19:00 and 22:00 to 03:00 local. Earlier, quantity-informed dosing is the only lever that addresses the start of that chain rather than its consequences, and it changes no insulin setting.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log the single largest recurring daytime eating occasion, recording approximate grams and the actual entry timestamp, for 7 to 10 consecutive days while changing nothing else; this simultaneously unblocks carb ratio assessment, produces the first COB series so the carbohydrate absorption model can be judged, and separates an afternoon basal shortfall from unannounced eating.

exceptions.suggestion: Treat existing insulin-on-board and the very low effective sensitivity in this window as already-committed insulin before adding any manual correction, and review these episodes with the care team rather than reacting within them.
exceptions.rationale: This window draws the most aggressive dosing of the day, with dynamic sensitivity of 27.8 to 42.5 mg/dL/U, temporary basal reaching the 4 U/h clamp and boosted SMB up to 1.6 U, and it is repeatedly followed by low glucose within 2 to 6 hours: 234 to 56 mg/dL at 120 minutes on 08-14, 264 to 96 mg/dL on 08-19, 206 to 53 mg/dL at 180 minutes on 08-16 and 165 to 78 mg/dL at 180 minutes on 08-11. The 08-19 episode is additionally confounded by occlusion and pump error announcements and should not be used as evidence about settings.

exceptions.suggestion: Note that added correction insulin in this window has the longest tail and the least support in the data, and discuss with the care team whether existing insulin-on-board already covers the elevation.
exceptions.rationale: Small late doses carry into the 10-hour DIA tail and land in the highest overnight low hours, where time below range is 11.4 percent at 00:00, 18.5 percent at 01:00 and about 10 percent at 02:00 and 03:00: 0.05 U at 125 mg/dL on 08-17 at 22:15 local was followed by 68 mg/dL at 180 minutes and 57 mg/dL at 240 minutes, 0.15 U at 138 mg/dL on 08-12 was followed by 82 mg/dL, and 0.05 U was added on 08-21 at 22:09 local while insulin-on-board was already 5.94 U. Frequent zero-rate temporary basals precede these lows, indicating that carried insulin rather than concurrent basal flow is responsible.

implementation_steps: Step 0, data and profile first: keep all 17 profile rows unchanged for now and confirm with the care team that the active profile in the package, with 7 basal segments totalling 16.2 U per day, a flat ISF of 56 mg/dL/U, five carb ratio segments, three target segments and a DIA of 10 hours, matches what is running on the pump, and note the profile switches on 08-13 when interpreting the first week.

Step 1, lowest-risk action and no insulin setting changed: begin logging one recurring daytime eating occasion with approximate grams and the actual entry timestamp for 7 to 10 consecutive days, changing nothing else, and observe whether the 10:00 to 17:00 local plateau flattens and whether peak insulin-on-board falls.

Step 2, automation second and one parameter only: discuss reducing max_iob_units from 25 U toward a range of roughly 6 to 8 U with the care team, confirming first whether total daily dose is nearer 20 or 36 U per day, then observe for 7 to 10 days specifically whether the level-2 lows at 18:00 to 19:00 local recur and whether time above range in the afternoon worsens.

Step 3, only if overshoot after high-glucose corrections persists with carbohydrates announced: discuss a single adjustment to dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent from 70 percent, changed alone and never together with max IOB, DIA or the profile ISF, and observe the same two local windows for 7 to 10 days.

Step 4, last resort and only if low glucose at 18:00 to 19:00 and 22:00 to 03:00 local persists after Steps 1 to 3: discuss reducing max_uam_smb_basal_minutes from 20 minutes, changed alone, while watching for a rebound increase in the 14:00 to 17:00 local plateau.

Step 5, deferred profile verification: on a day with no eating between 12:00 and 20:00 local and no manual correction, record glucose every 30 minutes to determine whether the afternoon rise and the early-evening fall persist without food; only a rise without food would support revisiting the 16:00 basal segment, and only persistent early-evening lows after Steps 1 to 4 would support revisiting the 19:00 segment.

Step 6, after carbohydrate logging exists: re-examine the carbohydrate absorption model (min_5m_carbimpact 8 and meal_max_absorption_hours 7) and the two carbohydrate-conditioned SMB flags, which are currently inert, and only then consider whether extended carbohydrates fit the observed absorption; do not combine this review with any step above.

Throughout: keep a written note of GLP-1 dosing days, since 1.25 mg was given on 08-14, 08-17 and 08-20 and overlaps the worst days, and of site, sensor, occlusion and pump-error events, so that confounded days can be excluded when judging any step.
education: Time in range of 86.0 percent and a coefficient of variation of 32.6 percent are both within commonly cited consensus targets, while time below range of 5.1 percent is above the commonly used 4 percent threshold; low-glucose exposure is generally addressed before high-glucose exposure when the two conflict.

When dynamic sensitivity is active, the profile ISF is one input to a calculation that scales with glucose and insulin-on-board rather than the sensitivity the loop actually applies; here the profile value of 56 mg/dL/U produced effective values from 27.8 to 124 mg/dL/U, which is why the profile row and the automation factor cannot be judged in isolation from one another.

A safety ceiling only protects when it is reachable. A max IOB of 25 U against an observed peak of 5.94 U never engaged, so it neither caused nor prevented anything; ceilings are usually sized with reference to actual daily insulin use.

A configured maximum SMB size acts as a base value that a build's boost logic can multiply. Logged standardMaxBolus of 0.2 U alongside delivered doses of 0.4 U and 1.6 U shows why the configured number should be read as a base rather than as a delivered limit.

With a 10-hour DIA, insulin delivered in the afternoon is still acting in the late evening and overnight. Low glucose occurring while basal delivery is already suspended points to insulin delivered hours earlier rather than to the basal rate in effect at that moment.

Unannounced meals force a closed loop to react after glucose has already risen, which routes meal coverage through the correction pathway at its most aggressive sensitivity. Announcing carbohydrates does not by itself add insulin; it changes when and on what basis the loop doses.

Extended carbohydrates in AAPS are a carbohydrate announcement spread over time that shapes carbohydrate-on-board and predictions. They are not a pump extended or dual-wave bolus and deliver no insulin on their own.

GLP-1 receptor agonists slow gastric emptying, which can flatten and prolong glucose excursions and change insulin needs. Doses on 08-14, 08-17 and 08-20 overlap the most variable days in this period, so day-to-day comparisons across those days are less reliable.

Correcting a single time window in isolation can shift a problem rather than solve it: adding insulin to the 14:00 to 17:00 local plateau would feed the 18:00 to 19:00 window that already carries 15.3 percent below range.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. It is not medical advice and it does not change any AAPS setting automatically.
Every proposed direction must be independently verified and agreed with the responsible diabetes care team before anything is altered.
Make only one change at a time and allow 7 to 10 days of observation before judging its effect, so that improvements or deteriorations can be attributed correctly.

Two sustained level-2 low episodes occurred in this period, on 08-13 reaching 42 mg/dL and on 08-14 reaching 41 mg/dL. Discuss these with the care team as a priority, ensure fast-acting carbohydrate is available, and monitor glucose closely at 18:00 to 19:00 and 22:00 to 03:00 local time.
No rescue carbohydrate or hypoglycaemia treatment was recorded in the period, so recovery from these episodes could not be assessed; logging treatments would improve future safety review.

Do not change dependent settings together. In particular, do not alter max IOB, the dynamic ISF factor, the SMB strength setting, DIA or the profile ISF in the same step, and note that raising the largest profile basal segment would also raise the automation safety clamp.

Insulin sensitivity, carbohydrate needs and insulin action vary with illness, activity, stress, GLP-1 dosing and site or sensor performance. If glucose behaviour changes unexpectedly, or if low glucose becomes more frequent or more severe at any point, contact the care team promptly rather than continuing a planned change sequence.

The analysis is based on a sample of the available telemetry, on a customised AAPS build whose boost, effective-target and sensitivity logic are not documented in the package, and on 14 days that include hardware faults on 08-19; conclusions should be treated as provisional and re-examined with fuller data.
